title: The Lines Look Wavy

patient.name: Mdm Yeo Poh Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: Noticed straight lines looking wavy in the left eye while checking her home Amsler grid

history.hpc: Mdm Yeo has dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and checks an Amsler grid at home. This week she noticed a change in the left eye. She says: 'The straight line on the grid, now look like got bend bend, wavy wavy, last time straight one.' She also feels the centre is a bit blurry. No pain, no redness. She came in promptly as advised.
history.pmhx: Dry AMD both eyes (left worse). Hypertension.
history.social_hx: Lives with daughter. Diligent with home Amsler monitoring. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal anterior segments; lens mild changes
examination_findings.fundus: Macular changes consistent with AMD; new distortion raises concern for progression — for doctor review

investigations.amsler_grid: Amsler grid tested in clinic: patient covers one eye, looks at the central dot, and reports any distortion, missing areas, or wavy lines. Left eye shows new metamorphopsia (wavy/bent lines) near the centre. This is an abnormal finding suggesting macular involvement and should be flagged.

diagnosis: New metamorphopsia on Amsler testing with reduced left-eye VA in a patient with AMD — concerning for progression (e.g., to wet AMD), which can need prompt treatment. The competency is correct Amsler administration, recognising the abnormal result, and timely escalation.

immediate: Administer the Amsler grid correctly: one eye covered, fixate the central dot, report distortion/missing areas/wavy lines
Test with the patient's reading correction if used, at the usual near distance, each eye separately
Recognise new wavy/bent lines (metamorphopsia) as an abnormal finding
Document the abnormal Amsler result and the reduced VA, comparing with previous VA
Flag promptly to the doctor, as new distortion in AMD can signal treatable progression
Reassure the patient and praise her prompt attendance
follow_up: Doctor to examine the macula and consider imaging (e.g., OCT) for possible wet AMD
If wet AMD is confirmed, prompt treatment (e.g., anti-VEGF) may be arranged
Reinforce continued home Amsler monitoring and prompt return for any change
patient_education: Explain that the wavy lines suggest a change at the macula that the doctor should review quickly
Praise her for monitoring at home and coming in promptly
Advise her to keep using the Amsler grid for each eye separately and to return urgently if distortion worsens
Reassure her that prompt review gives the best chance to act if treatment is needed

key_points: Establishes the new onset of distortion in the left eye
Confirms the known AMD and home Amsler monitoring habit
Notes associated central blurring and absence of pain/redness
Acknowledges her prompt attendance as advised
Administers the Amsler grid correctly (one eye, central fixation, near distance, with correction)
Tests each eye separately and asks specifically about distortion/missing areas
Performs VA and compares with the previous reading
Documents the abnormal Amsler finding and reduced VA
Recognises new metamorphopsia as an abnormal macular sign
Understands new distortion in AMD can indicate treatable progression (wet AMD)
Links the Amsler finding with the reduced VA
Flags the abnormal result promptly to the doctor
Documents the Amsler result and VA comparison
Reinforces continued home monitoring and urgent return advice
Reassures and praises the patient appropriately
